items.text: Review RFIs, changes and coordination drawings

Record meeting and approval to begin

path: Initial phase — when, where and how

items.text: Compare work to mockup or sample

Record results and authorize continued production

groups.title: Follow-up phase — when, where and how
path: Follow-up phase — when, where and how

Repeat testing and inspection as required
Continue until the feature is complete and accepted

Break project into separately controlled work features
Link each feature to CSI division and schedule activity

path: Receiving inspection — when, where and how

items.text: Verify purchase order and approved submittal

groups.title: Doors, frames, hardware and glazing quality
path: Doors, frames, hardware and glazing quality

items.text: Verify glazing type and safety markings
Verify door, elevator, HVAC and generator interfaces
Identify hold point in the inspection and test plan
Stop work at the defined point
Apply contract rule if witness declines or misses the event
Do not confuse a witness point with a hold point
Every weld or defined weld sample
Assess prior results after failed calibration
Obtain required design or owner approval
Repair, rework, replace, reject or accept by formal concession
Use as is with formal authorized acceptance
Link every definable feature to preparatory, initial and follow-up controls when applicable.
Schedule quality activities before irreversible work.
Include testing, report turnaround and retesting.
Preserve hold points and do not bypass required releases.
Tie deficiencies to corrective work and affected successors.
Repeat the initial phase when crews, methods or conditions materially change.
Track quality at fabrication, delivery, storage and installation.
Integrate quality control with safety, inspections, testing, commissioning and closeout.
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, ER 1180-1-6, Construction Quality Management, 2025 — identifies preparatory, initial and follow-up phases as the core three-phase control system.
